subject: Cloud Computing
title: When to Choose PaaS
description: One-minute skill: When to Choose PaaS.

hook.text: Your small team wants to ship fast. Managing servers would consume half your engineering time.

buildup.text: PaaS is best when developer speed matters more than infrastructure control.

discovery.text: Startups, prototypes, and small teams thrive on PaaS. Less ops work means more product work.

twist.text: But if you outgrow the platform's limits, migrating away can be as painful as rebuilding from scratch.

climax.text: PaaS buys you speed now at the potential cost of flexibility later. That trade-off is often worth it.

punchline.text: Choose PaaS when shipping fast matters most. Worry later.

quiz.question: What type of team benefits most from PaaS?
options: Small teams that need to ship quickly without managing infrastructure
Large enterprises with dedicated infrastructure departments
Teams that need to customize every aspect of their server setup

details.summary: Choose PaaS when your team wants to focus on application development without managing infrastructure. It excels for web applications, APIs, and microservices where standard runtimes suffice and rapid iteration matters more than low-level control.
details.whyItMatters: PaaS maximizes developer productivity for suitable workloads. Choosing it correctly saves significant operational effort compared to managing IaaS for workloads that do not need it.
takeaways: Best for web apps and APIs using standard runtimes
Ideal for small teams without dedicated infrastructure staff
Choose when rapid iteration outweighs low-level control needs

faq.question: When should you avoid PaaS?
faq.answer: Avoid PaaS for workloads needing custom kernel configurations, specific OS-level dependencies, or extremely fine-grained resource control. Long-running background jobs, GPU workloads, and applications with unusual networking requirements may not fit PaaS constraints.

faq.question: Is PaaS more expensive than IaaS?
faq.answer: PaaS costs more per unit of compute than equivalent IaaS resources because you pay for management overhead. However, the total cost including engineering time is often lower because your team spends less time on infrastructure operations.
